pages.text: The Brusselator, the simplest model of the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction: X makes more X from Y, and is used up again. Its steady state turns unstable - and the mixture starts to oscillate - only when B > 1 + A² (a Hopf bifurcation). Just past it, the beat has a period near 2π/A.
$(thing)Set$(): Bromate feed A, Malonic acid feed B.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Stirring: the threshold varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The further past the threshold, the more clocks.
